summary: This paper proposes NOBOL, a method for implementing logical CNOT gates between distant qubits encoded in arbitrary CSS codes using only a single Bell pair and local operations. The approach achieves logarithmic circuit depth $O(\log \tau)$ where $\tau$ is the weight of the logical operator, reducing the entanglement overhead from linear in code size $N$ to a single shared pair.
motivation: Standard logical CNOT operations between distant qubits require linear overhead: either $O(N)$ SWAP operations in monolithic systems or $O(N)$ Bell pairs in distributed quantum computing, with lattice surgery requiring $O(d^2)$ pairs for 2D surface codes. This entanglement bottleneck severely limits scalability of distributed quantum architectures.
method: NOBOL generalizes the physical remote CNOT primitive (using one Bell pair and LOCC) to the logical level by exploiting the fact that logical operations need only act on the support of logical operators. A CNOT between single qubit $q$ and logical qubit $B_L$ uses $2\tau_B - 1$ CNOTs on the $\tau_B$ qubits in $B_X^L$; a CZ between $q'$ and $A_L$ similarly uses the $\tau_A$ qubits in $A_Z^L$. Algorithms 1 and 2 construct depth-optimal circuits achieving $O(\log \tau)$ depth through recursive binary tree structures.
result: The method requires only one Bell pair independent of code distance, compared to $O(d^2)$ for surface codes via lattice surgery. Error containment strategies using small repetition codes on the Bell pair qubits and intermittent adaptive stabilization (tracking predictable stabilizer evolution) suppress error propagation at the cost of $O(\tau_B d)$ depth for stabilization or additional ancillas for encoding. The approach is agnostic to qubit modality and applicable to all CSS codes.
